## Classes

### <a name="patchbot"></a>`patchbot`

This is the **pull path** for patch posture: `include patchbot` and, on its
next Puppet run, the `patchbot` external fact
(available/security/reboot_required) reaches the console via PuppetDB — the
Patching page and Action Center read it with no Bolt push.

The fact script itself ships in the module's `facts.d/` and is delivered to
agents by pluginsync; this class only guarantees the OS package metadata the
fact counts against stays reasonably fresh, so the numbers are meaningful
between agent runs.

The active `patchbot::patch` Bolt task (console "Patch" button) is the push
complement; it does not need this class.

Dependency-light on purpose: manages the refresh timer with native systemd
unit files (no puppet/systemd dependency), so the module pins nothing.
Windows is a deliberate no-op here (the $refresh_cmd selector below has no
'windows' branch, so this class manages nothing on Windows nodes) — Windows
Update maintains its own metadata, there's no apt/dnf-style local cache to
refresh, and facts.d/patchbot.ps1 queries WUA live on every fact run.

#### Examples

##### 

```puppet
include patchbot
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `patchbot` class:

* [`manage_cache`](#-patchbot--manage_cache)
* [`cache_refresh`](#-patchbot--cache_refresh)

##### <a name="-patchbot--manage_cache"></a>`manage_cache`

Data type: `Boolean`

Keep the package manager's update metadata fresh (a small systemd timer)
so the fact's counts are current. Default true.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-patchbot--cache_refresh"></a>`cache_refresh`

Data type: `String[1]`

systemd OnCalendar expression for the refresh timer. Default 'daily'.

Default value: `'daily'`

## Tasks

### <a name="patch"></a>`patch`

Apply available OS updates (all, security-only, or a specific set of patch_ids) on a node, optionally reboot when required, then refresh the patchbot posture. The console reads the resulting posture via the patchbot fact on the next run. Dispatches to the POSIX (patch.sh) or Windows (patch.ps1) implementation automatically based on the target.

**Supports noop?** false

#### Parameters

##### `console_url`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Console base URL (server-injected; unused by the patch itself).

##### `ingest_token`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Server-injected; unused by the patch itself.

##### `security_only`

Data type: `Boolean`

Apply only security updates when true; otherwise apply all available updates. Ignored when patch_ids is set.

##### `patch_ids`

Data type: `Optional[Array[Pattern[/\A[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:+-]*\z/]]]`

Install only these specific patch/package ids, as reported in the patchbot fact's patches[] array (KB numbers on Windows, package names on Linux). Takes priority over security_only when set. Must match [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:+-]* -- rejected otherwise, since these are used unquoted on a package-manager command line running as root and a leading '-' or embedded whitespace would be read as a flag, not a package name.

##### `reboot`

Data type: `Boolean`

Reboot the node afterward if a reboot is required.
